Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

redlinebench · has stage: RedlineBench gives the agent a party-specific playbook, commercial context and a source contract: a clean template at Turn 1 and a previously redlined draft with tracked changes visible at Turn 2 and later. The agent produces a native Word redline with tracked edits and comments; counterparty playbooks and verifier-side rubrics are not visible to the agent.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.redlinebench.agent-workflow.v3

  • Two acceptance-only final-turn tasks intentionally lack an attorney golden redline; golden files support document-native behavioral metrics rather than being agent inputs.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

redlinebench · human annotation: RedlineBench’s source report describes independently branching attorney negotiation paths and rubrics authored around the most important redline decisions; the creator card says senior technology-transactions attorneys wrote weighted criteria in real time as they negotiated each turn.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.redlinebench.attorney-rubrics.v2

  • The five rubric dimensions cover legal correctness, commercial context, negotiation quality, counterparty acceptance anddeal-closing orientation; they encode contextual judgments rather than a universal single correct redline.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

redlinebench · evaluates: The RedlineBench README describes a loadable-Word-output validity gate, weighted rubric scores with penalties clipped to zero through one, and strict-majority voting by a three-LLM panel; the card aggregates within input groups and then equally across twelve scenario-by-turn cells.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.redlinebench.scoring.v2

  • The source report separately computes behavioral metrics directly from document edits without LLM judges. Reproduction is non-deterministic because of agent sampling and LLM judging.

redlinebench · dataset size: RedlineBench’s creator README defines 140 runnable tasks across three negotiation scenarios and four turns; tasks in the same input group share model-facing input but differ in the attorney rubric set used to grade it.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.redlinebench.units.v2

  • A rubric variant is not a new underlying negotiation input or an independent benchmark family.
